principle_text: When the persuadee expresses a preference for addressing other issues or donating to different organizations, avoid insisting on a specific charity that does not align with their priorities.
When the persuadee shares personal information unrelated to the cause, avoid shifting the conversation without linking it back to the charitable goal or donation appeal.
When the persuadee expresses general agreement without commitment, avoid giving only compliments without connecting to specific actions or donation opportunities.
When the persuadee indicates they have recently donated to a related cause, avoid asking if they have ever thought about donating, as it may not increase their willingness to donate again.
When the persuadee expresses positive feelings about a group in need, you should directly connect those feelings to the opportunity to help through donations.
When the persuadee expresses concern about the well-being of a vulnerable group, you should highlight the importance of caring for that group to increase empathy and willingness to donate.
When the persuadee expresses general concern for a cause, you should focus on specific, emotionally impactful issues to deepen their engagement and elicit stronger empathetic responses.
When the persuadee shows initial awareness of a charity, you should invite them to learn more by highlighting the charity's mission and asking if they want additional information.
When the persuadee shows personal connection to the cause, you should raise awareness about the scale of the problem to encourage acknowledgment and increase willingness to donate.
When the persuadee shows some awareness of the issue, you should confirm their understanding and introduce a credible organization to increase their receptiveness to donating.
